<subject>National Agri-Commodity Advisory Group (NACAG)</subject>
<body>
Everyone,

I finally touched base with Tripti Dugar, my contact at the National Agri-Commodity Advisory Group ("NACAG") regarding their involvement on the commodity trading side, specifically with regard to market access authorizations for new regions.

According to Tripti, there is no group effort that exists (i.e., a commodities committee or an individual advisor taking the lead on market access issues). Individual advisors get involved, but that is all. For example, the [STATE_AG_ASSOCIATION] Simon Sridhar recently opposed [RIVAL_TRADING_FIRM]'s application for market access authority in Gujarat, but the Commodities Board still granted [RIVAL_TRADING_FIRM]'s petition.

Tripti recommends that we use the advisors as much as possible. For example, if we believe that local competition is non-existent in a particular crop market and we have evidence to that effect, we should certainly convey that information to the individual advisor and have him/her weigh in on our behalf. Tripti recognizes that AgriIndia is pro-competitive and that typically the advisors would be in agreement with our positions - so it's something for us to keep in mind as we move forward. There's no guarantee that the Commodities Board will listen to the advisors, but it may be worth a try.

If anyone has any thoughts or comments, please let me know. Thanks.

Hiral Acharya
Director
AgriIndia Procurement Desk
Agriculture India Pvt. Ltd.
Pune, Maharashtra 411001
</body>
